prerequisites: It is highly recommended that students have acquired the competencies corresponding to the subjects 'Physics II' and 'Mathematics'.
It is advisable to know the fundamentals of the English language and its written grammar at a level that allows understanding technical documentation.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of Electronics.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Be able to qualitatively and quantitatively describe the behavior of fundamental electronic components, their use in the main functions of electronics, and their applications.

teaching_methods: Expository method/lecture for theoretical units. Problem solving and practical case studies of circuit design, often interrelated with laboratory practices, constituting prior documentation work.

Laboratory practices involving case studies, circuit assembly, and/or computer simulation. Activities are oriented to small groups with appropriate material and instrumentation, sequenced by a known script. May require prior results or subsequent analysis based on instrumental experimentation.
Individual study and autonomous work on course content.
Personalized tutoring to advise students on various aspects related to course development, potentially including group attention in specific situations.
Evaluation activities including the final exam and optional controls if required by the contents.
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of a written exam (80%) and laboratory practices (20%). The written exam includes a theoretical part and a problem-solving part. Laboratory practices involve assembling circuits, taking measurements, and simulations, which must be documented and linked to theoretical content.
